# Storage inventory for ISSUE-392

Provide an operator-only, read-only `swarm storage report` command, with `--json` for automation, across registered repositories, the selected checkout, managed cache roots and scratch. This command is proposed here and must be implemented before it is documented. It reports observations and conservative eligibility; it neither authorizes nor performs reclamation.

## Dimensions and boundaries

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / standard; approved profile: detailed. Keep GitHub and local backends, Linux/macOS, native Codex and harness-tools Bubblewrap in scope. No deletion, eviction, warning settings, maintenance settings, OCI garbage collection, remote archival, new mounts or producer lifecycle retrofit. Estimated plan/implementation/validation effort is 10–14 hours, within the 16-hour claim budget; platform and live-service checks remain a PR checklist. Human plan approval is required before implementation.

## What we know

- Cache owners and layouts are explicit: `internal/sandbox/build_cache.go:36` defines separate agent/validator owners; `repositoryCacheKey` at line 118 hashes the canonical Git common directory; `persistentBuildCaches` at line 195 uses owner/key/ecosystem; `migrateLegacyGoCache` at line 235 recognizes former go-build/key storage. Do not call preparation or migration during inventory.
- Dependency owners are agent-deps and validate-deps (`internal/sandbox/dependency_cache.go:91`); `PrepareDependencyCaches` at line 254 performs preparation/prefetch and is unsuitable for inspection.
- #391 supplies durable use evidence and deliberately leaves crash-interrupted uses unresolved (`internal/storageuse/storage.go:1`). `Open`, `AcquireUse`, and maintenance locking create directories/files. Repository-wide search for storageuse in non-test Go files found only its own package: current producer integration cannot be presumed. Missing records must remain unknown.
- Even registry reads create directories and a lock through `withLock` (`internal/registry/registry.go:72`, `List` at line 211). Inventory needs a non-creating reader, including in CLI pre-run resolution.
- `DiscoverCleanupWorktrees` (`internal/workspace/cleanup_inventory.go:40`) unions physical paths and Git registrations but uses whole-directory and whole-command reads. `InspectCleanupWorktree` (`internal/workspace/cleanup.go:65`) checks registration, expected head, dirtiness, nested repos and retained invoking checkout, but also has unbounded reads/walks. Reuse its rules, not an unbounded invocation.
- `SnapshotCleanup` and `InspectCleanupSnapshot` (`internal/lease/cleanup_bulk.go:28,69`) share PR evidence; authoritative issue linkage, rather than PR body hints, is required (`ResolveCleanupWorktrees`, line 111). Existing list APIs return complete slices (`internal/tracker/github.go:779`, `internal/tracker/local.go:663`). Bounded reporting needs an incremental listing path.
- `Manager.loadReadOnly` (`internal/lease/manager.go:387`) and `LoadCheckpointPreview` (`internal/coordination/store.go:101,291`) provide preview-oriented state access. Check all transitive calls for allocations, fetches and lock creation before using them.
- Scratch producers include worker (`internal/sandbox/worker.go:376`), native (`internal/sandbox/native.go:651`), prefetch (`internal/sandbox/node_prefetch.go:86`, `dependency_cache.go:587,1031`, `dependency_cache_python.go:59`), validation (`internal/validation/validator.go:304`) and review (`internal/agent/review.go:47`). Prefixes identify candidates only.
- `make check` runs formatting checks, vet, staticcheck, race tests and fragment validation (`Makefile:37–49`). This explicit acceptance requirement is separate from coordinator claim-bound validation.

## What we're assuming

- Default host coverage should include the current selected repository plus the registry, user-cache/swarm and the effective OS temporary directory. Validate this against layout fixtures and all in-scope producer call sites in step 1. No recursive whole-home or whole-disk search.
- Ownership can sometimes be proven from an existing repository's canonical common-dir hash even without an index. A matching key proves cache association, not complete use coverage or abandonment; test these independently.
- The 64 MiB limit means retained inventory working data and bounded in-flight input/output buffers, not the entire Go runtime RSS. Use conservative accounting including strings, maps, slices, parser buffers and queues, with deterministic test counters; stop before admitting data beyond the budget.

## Open questions

- Parent #378 sections A–D are not bundled or present in the searchable checkout, and no GitHub connector is available in this session. The contract governs this plan. Reviewer should reconcile the parent context when available; no live-GitHub prerequisite is added to implementation.
- There is no confirmed discoverable production storageuse control-root convention or producer coverage. Step 1 will search the implementation checkout again and design a read-only observation API for supplied, trusted coordinator roots. Without such evidence report unknown; do not invent paths or create registry records. Reopen if acceptance is interpreted as requiring producer integration beyond #391's delivered primitives.
- Exact positive legacy evidence available on disk is answered by layout fixtures in step 2. Unverifiable scratch and orphan keys stay visible with unknown owner/activity/eligibility; disappearance of a repository is not proof of abandonment.
- Linux/macOS allocated-block/inode representation and filesystem atime behavior need platform review. Reads cannot promise to suppress filesystem-maintained atime on all supported mounts; tests prove unchanged contents, names, permissions, mtime, registry/recency and workflow state. Document this distinction in review evidence, and flag a literal atime-preservation interpretation for the human gate.

## Architecture and report semantics

Create `internal/storage` as a coordinator-side inventory service. CLI supplies trusted discovery roots and bounded read-only backend adapters. No dependencies on worker runtime execution, cleanup/apply paths or candidate-selected tools. Use safefs directory/regular opens without creation; reject symlinks, special files and unsafe parent components. Resource paths are display data, never executable commands or authority.

Each report has schema version, snapshot scope, completeness, limits/counters and incomplete reasons. Each resource has repository/cache owner (explicit unknown allowed), class, path (refs have repository plus ref name), identity, logical usage or null plus reason, optional allocated usage, last-use/retention evidence and source, tri-state active status, eligibility (`eligible`, `retained`, `blocked`, `unknown`) and reason. Evidence is an observation, not an atomic global snapshot. Stable rendering for identical inputs; unknown never serializes as zero or inactive. Do not infer last-use from directory mtime. Unresolved use tokens block; missing/corrupt/incomplete use coverage makes eligibility unknown. Never expose raw use tokens or credentials.

Confirm the proposed defaults: 256 unique repositories, 10,000 resource records, 100,000 filesystem entries, 100,000 distinct inode identities, 64 MiB accounted working data, at most two filesystem workers; check cancellation before work, at every page/buffer boundary and at least every 128 entries. A single shared budget covers discovery, state, registry, Git output, PR pages, walking, dedup and rendering. Use fixed-size directory reads, bounded queues and bounded strings/records; reject an oversized record before decoding it. Bound parser nesting and Git/API buffers as well. Stream or boundedly decode registry entries and local backend records; do not decode an arbitrarily large YAML/JSON document and truncate afterward. Limit reached, cancellation, permission failure or malformed input emits available partial output with explicit incompleteness and affected usage/eligibility unknown. Fatal invocation/output errors return errors; cancellation returns cancellation after emitting partial output where the writer still works. Ordinary incomplete scans return success with conspicuous complete=false in both formats.

Deduplicate physical observations globally by device/inode on Linux/macOS, and resource aliases by canonical identity. Track logical bytes separately from allocated blocks; sparse/compressed/cloned data and hardlinks outside the snapshot mean allocated bytes are observations, not guaranteed savings. Give branches no independent byte-saving total; shared Git objects belong to a repository shared-storage record counted once, never charged per branch/worktree. Preserve per-resource logical usage when safely measurable, but never sum it as reclaimable physical bytes. When dedup coverage is exhausted or unsupported, stop physical aggregation and label unknown, retaining partial observed values only as such. No claim of physical reclaimability in this part.

## Exact touchpoints

Modify existing files only where needed:

- `internal/cli/root.go`: register `newStorageCmd`; bypass repository-required normalization for host inventory and avoid registry Get/List side effects in its pre-run. Preserve validation and existing commands.
- `internal/registry/registry.go`: add bounded non-creating `ReadSnapshot` API, distinct from existing locking CRUD.
- `internal/storageuse/storage.go`: add bounded read-only snapshot/observation entry point that opens existing control roots only, validates version/resource/key and does not acquire maintenance/use locks or update recency. Keep existing mutation and exclusion behavior unchanged.
- `internal/workspace/cleanup_inventory.go`, `cleanup.go`: add budget-aware read-only inventory/inspection variants with bounded Git output and streaming directory reads; retain existing cleanup callers and their behavior.
- `internal/lease/cleanup_bulk.go`, `cleanup_preview.go`: expose a bounded inventory snapshot/inspection path that shares one PR traversal and uses authoritative read-only issue state; do not weaken cleanup safety or invoke mutation methods.
- `internal/tracker/tracker.go`, `github.go`, `local.go`: add an optional bounded PR-visitor capability with completeness/error result; retain existing Tracker interface compatibility via a separate optional interface. GitHub implementation pages once, local implementation streams bounded existing records without initializing storage. Unavailable capability means eligibility unknown, not fallback to unlimited listing.
- `internal/coordination/store.go`: add a bounded preview read only if existing preview paths cannot accept the remaining budget without allocating beyond it; preserve CAS/write paths.
- Existing tests to extend where those APIs change: `internal/registry/registry_test.go`, `internal/storageuse/storage_test.go`, `internal/workspace/cleanup_inventory_test.go`, `cleanup_test.go`, `internal/lease/cleanup_bulk_test.go`, `internal/tracker/pr_list_test.go`, `internal/coordination/store_test.go`, `internal/cli/managed_root_test.go` and `root_test.go`.
- `docs/project.md`: operator inventory usage adjacent to existing cache ownership explanation. No new settings; update CLI examples only after implementation/help verification.

Proposed new files (absent from the supplied approved-source snapshot): `internal/storage/inventory.go` (Snapshot, Resource, Limits, Scan), `discovery.go` (layout/owner adapters), `accounting.go` (Budget and bounded traversal), `stat_unix.go` (Linux/macOS inode/block identity with build tags), `stat_other.go` (explicit unsupported result), `inventory_test.go`, `discovery_test.go`, `accounting_test.go`; `internal/cli/storage.go` (newStorageCmd/renderStorageReport), `storage_test.go`; `changes/unreleased/392.md`. All internal/storage paths are under that new directory. This environment has no .git metadata, so absence is confirmed against the supplied source tree, not `git cat-file`; developer must confirm absence at approved base_sha before adding files and treat any existing file as modified. No protected files change.

## Implementation sequence

1. Verify approved source/parent context when available; map trusted roots and every in-scope layout, backend read and pre-run dependency. Confirm new-file absence at base_sha. Establish limits, schema and injected adapters first. Inventory must work outside a checkout using host roots and an absent registry. Do not initialize repositories or resolve authenticated managers merely to scan cache entries.
2. Implement bounded registry and use-evidence observations, then discovery over registered/selected repositories, cache owner roots and scratch candidate roots. Union indexed records with actual bounded directory entries so unindexed resources/orphan keys remain visible. Match existing common-dir identities; validate proven legacy go-build fixtures; do not migrate. Never follow arbitrary record locations outside trusted roots. Prefix-only scratch gets an unknown record rather than an abandoned/eligible verdict.
3. Implement bounded filesystem accounting, hardlink dedup, overlap handling, platform-stat abstraction, partial results and cancellation. Aggregate shared Git storage separately. Budget every adapter and parser allocation before admitting input, not after building output slices.
4. Implement bounded worktree/ref discovery including branches whose worktree has disappeared, issue/PR registrations whose directory has disappeared, and physical unregistered entries. Link to authoritative state; inspect dirty/locked/invoking/active-claim/pending-submission/revision resources conservatively. Use one bounded paginated PR traversal per repository only where repository eligibility needs it, zero remote calls for cache/scratch. Offline/truncated/unavailable state cannot grant eligibility. Do not fetch refs, prune, refresh indexes, create tracker stores or authorize actions. Bound Git subprocess stdout/stderr and terminate promptly on context cancellation.
5. Add CLI wiring, human rendering and JSON using the same snapshot. Human output calls out partial/unknown evidence. JSON includes all required fields even when null. `--repo`/`--root` narrow repository selection using non-creating lookup; default is all known repositories plus selected checkout when available; cache/scratch orphans remain host-wide and scope is printed. Reject `--fork` for this coordinator-only command; no worker gateway access or new credentials. No apply option.
6. Add acceptance/regression fixtures and operator docs/fragment. Run developer focused checks; tester independently checks source, tests and coverage, reusing passing results. Complete make check once on the final candidate under the responsibility described in TEST_PLAN.md. Record unavailable host/live checks in PR checklist without expanding the scope or blocking sandbox-verifiable implementation.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source; approved WorkUnit, trusted policy and human gate remain authoritative.

Entry points: `newRootCmdWithOptions` (`internal/cli/root.go:68`), `normalizeCoordinatorRoot` (`root.go:286`), registry `withLock` (`internal/registry/registry.go:72`), storageuse `Open` (`internal/storageuse/storage.go:60`), `DiscoverCleanupWorktrees` (`internal/workspace/cleanup_inventory.go:40`), `InspectCleanupWorktree` (`internal/workspace/cleanup.go:65`), `SnapshotCleanup`/`InspectCleanupSnapshot` (`internal/lease/cleanup_bulk.go:28,69`), backend PR listings (`internal/tracker/github.go:779`, `local.go:663`), preview storage (`internal/coordination/store.go:101,291`). Verify line positions before editing.

Extend existing cleanup, registry, storageuse and PR-list fixtures listed above. Add small synthetic FS/page/allocator adapters in internal/storage tests; keep real temp-dir/hardlink/Git fixtures for integration. Focused commands:

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/registry ./internal/workspace ./internal/lease ./internal/tracker ./internal/coordination ./internal/cli
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse
go vet ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/registry ./internal/workspace ./internal/lease ./internal/tracker ./internal/coordination ./internal/cli
gofmt -l internal/storage internal/cli/storage.go internal/cli/storage_test.go
make check
```

Include all changed existing Go files in format diagnostics. Tests are planned commands, not results from this planning run. The tester reuses applicable successful developer commands; repeats require relevant changes, failures or unresolved coverage concerns.

Checked assumptions: separate cache owners/common-dir hashes inspected in build_cache.go; prefix-only scratch producers inspected; registry reads and storageuse opens confirmed creating; no storageuse producer calls found by non-test source search; no .git metadata available; parent plan absent from provided files. Recheck the implementation checkout for differences.

Reopen for human review if eligibility requires inventing missing use coverage, new registration/lifecycle writes, protected-file edits, platform privilege/mount changes, a broader disk search, changed cleanup authority, or inability to bound the streaming backend reads within this cycle. Unknown legacy/orphan reporting is expected, not a reason to expand scope.

**What this change breaks** (repository searches and planned compatibility):

- `internal/registry/registry_test.go` relies on existing CRUD/locking: preserve unchanged; add separate no-create reader tests.
- `internal/storageuse/storage_test.go` and `crash_unix_test.go` assert durable unresolved uses/exclusion: preserve unchanged; read observations never complete a use.
- `internal/workspace/cleanup_test.go`, `cleanup_inventory_test.go`, `internal/lease/cleanup_bulk_test.go`, `internal/cli/cleanup_bulk_test.go` cover existing cleanup eligibility and one-list behavior: preserve current command/schema/apply behavior; new bounded APIs must not weaken those checks.
- Tracker implementers/fakes (including `internal/lease/cleanup_bulk_test.go` countingCleanupTracker and lifecycle fixtures) implement the current interface: preserve interface compatibility with optional bounded capability; add inventory-specific fakes.
- Root help gains a resource command (`internal/cli/root.go:125`); inspect root/managed-root tests for exact command lists and extend only expectations affected by storage report. Existing other-command pre-run behavior remains unchanged.
- `docs/project.md` cache-layout and ownership tables remain accurate; append report instructions and logical/allocated/unknown explanations. `README.md`, harness guides, templates, prompts, config and all protected files remain unchanged.
- `changes/unreleased/391.md` describes primitives only: preserve unchanged; add the distinct 392 operator feature fragment. No existing production caller is renamed or removed.

# ISSUE-392 acceptance and verification

Commands below are planned, not already passing results. Use isolated temporary roots and local/HTTP fixtures; never inspect or mutate the operator's real home in tests. Developer owns focused implementation checks. Tester independently reads changed source and each criterion, reviews fixture quality and reuses applicable passing developer results. Repeat only after relevant source changes, observed failure or unresolved coverage concern.

## Acceptance mapping

| Criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| 1. All storage classes, unindexed and orphan storage, human/JSON | Table-driven inventory fixtures for agent-build and validate-build (Go/Rust/C++), legacy go-build, agent-deps and validate-deps across implemented ecosystem table, issue/PR physical and registered worktrees, code branches with/without a worktree, shared Git objects, worker/native sandbox, prefetch (including nested Rust staging), validation and review scratch. Include empty/absent registry, unindexed valid key, orphan key, missing repo, duplicate registry aliases, unknown entry and invocation outside Git. CLI tests compare both renderers against the same snapshot and assert every class survives. Run focused package command below. |
| 2. Required per-resource fields | Assert owner/class/path/ref, logical/allocated usage or explicit null/reason, last-use or retention evidence/source, tri-state active, eligibility and blocked/retained reason. Test completed uses, unresolved/crashed uses, incomplete coverage, absent/malformed records, moving files, permission failures, dirty/locked/invoking worktrees, active claims, submission/revision state and offline/truncated PR state. Absence never becomes zero usage, inactive or safe; directory mtime never becomes last-use evidence. JSON schema assertions and human-output assertions use the same fixtures. |
| 3. No mutations | Before/after snapshots of names, file types, permissions, contents/hashes, mtime, refs, Git index/config/worktree registrations, registry and lock-file existence, durable use recency, local coordination files, tracker state and workflow/lease/artifact state. Invoke both human and JSON reports, including first run with absent control roots, missing registry and missing lock files. HTTP fixture records methods and rejects mutations; assert no fetch/prune/refresh/init/cleanup subprocesses and no use/maintenance/registry mutation APIs. Repeat for errors, cancellation and limit exits. Explicitly exclude OS-maintained atime from equality; flag any literal atime requirement for gate review per PLAN. No symlink/special-file escape or fake Git hook execution. |
| 4. Shared and hardlinked accounting | Real two-resource hardlink fixture plus synthetic cross-device equal-inode fixture, repeated paths, parent/child overlap, sparse file, external hardlink and dedup-cap exhaustion. Logical per-resource usage may repeat; unique allocation aggregate counts observed identity once; physical savings are never asserted. Git fixture has two issue/PR worktrees and branches sharing object storage; branches have no independent savings and shared storage appears once. Platform-stat fixtures cover Linux/macOS block fields and unsupported stat results. |
| 5. Proven legacy and unproven orphans | Positive legacy go-build fixture matches a real canonical common-dir key and private safe directory layout. Negative cases: matching prefix alone, invalid/mismatched key, removed repository, malformed/candidate-authored metadata, symlink parents, unsafe permissions and unknown scratch prefix. Matching ownership without use coverage still has unknown eligibility. Assert visibility and no migration/rename/new index. |
| 6. Bounds, cancellation, partial output | Inject lazy directory/registry/state/Git/API iterators, accounted allocator and worker scheduler, not huge directories or wall-clock benchmarks. For each cap test below/at/above boundary: 256 repos, 10,000 records, 100,000 entries, 100,000 inode identities, 64 MiB working data, two workers and cancellation within 128 entries. Count attempted admissions and reads as well as emitted data. Include huge single names/documents, deeply nested input, wide directories, oversized Git stdout/stderr, API pages and record fields. Assert no over-budget materialization before truncation. Assert one paginated PR traversal/repo, zero cache-triggered remote calls, page/byte caps and no per-resource fallback queries; API truncation/offline makes eligibility unknown. Mid-walk/page/parse cancellation emits valid partial JSON/human incomplete output and returns cancellation. No invented grand totals or physical savings. |
| 7. Docs, fragment and checks | Check implemented Cobra registration/help against docs/project.md examples, confirm no invented settings/flags, check relative links and bash snippets, validate changes/unreleased/392.md with changelog tool. Run focused packages and make check. Review Linux/macOS unavailable integration items in PR checklist. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

Run as affected packages are ready and retain command/results with the source revision:

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/registry ./internal/workspace ./internal/lease ./internal/tracker ./internal/coordination ./internal/cli
go test -race -timeout=5m ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse
go vet ./internal/storage ./internal/storageuse ./internal/registry ./internal/workspace ./internal/lease ./internal/tracker ./internal/coordination ./internal/cli
gofmt -l internal/storage internal/cli/storage.go internal/cli/storage_test.go
go run ./cmd/swarm storage report --help
go run ./cmd/changelog --check
```

Add changed existing Go files to gofmt diagnostics. Test CLI report execution with injected roots/backends, not real host caches. Parse any added bash snippets with `bash -n` using a temporary extracted file; resolve added relative links. Run race tests for additional changed concurrent components if review identifies a gap. The full acceptance-required final check is `make check`; run it once on the final candidate and retain its result rather than rerunning it separately per role. An unavailable runtime/tool must be recorded as a verification limitation, never called a pass.

## Tester-owned independent review

Trace discovery coverage back to real producers, table definitions and authoritative read paths; do not treat the plan's proposed APIs as already present. Verify non-creating CLI pre-run, registry reads, local tracker construction, Git preview and storageuse reads transitively. Confirm bounded input parsing and all queues/maps/output buffers, not just final slice lengths. Review positive tests for eligibility and adversarial tests where apparently familiar layouts remain unknown. Verify no contributor data, prefix, missing path or elapsed lease alone grants authority. Inspect shared-object attribution and renderer wording separately from numeric correctness.

Reuse successful developer commands when source and coverage still apply. Run targeted failing/missing cases or changed-package format/static diagnostics only when source changes, failures or specific unresolved coverage justify them. Record remaining platform/service limitations and acceptance disposition; do not quietly omit a criterion.

## Coordinator-owned policy and publication

The complete approved-base required policy in SYSTEM_PROMPT.md is a coordinator-owned reference, not a per-role command list. Coordinator runs it once after roles finish against the final candidate. Agent results are advisory and do not satisfy claim-bound validation or publication. The explicit WorkUnit `make check` result may be recorded alongside coordinator checks, but does not replace them. Human plan approval and all fenced state/publication operations stay with the coordinator/independent maintainer; do not acquire credentials from this planning/testing session.

## PR review checklist for unavailable environments

- On macOS, validate stat identity/block adapter and non-creating scan behavior with the same fixtures; review OS temporary/cache root resolution and filesystem atime expectations.
- On Linux native Codex and harness-tools Bubblewrap hosts, compare representative cache/scratch report observations with producer paths and existing unresolved-use evidence. No new mount or execution permission is needed to report storage.
- With GitHub operator access, confirm one bounded paginated PR traversal and offline/truncated behavior against a representative repository; HTTP fixture tests cover this in the sandbox. Local backend tests need no live service.
- Reconcile parent #378 A–D when accessible. Missing producer use coverage remains unknown in this part; producer integration/deletion/maintenance changes need separate scope approval.

# Implementation Summary (Issue #392)

## What we learned

- The coordinator Git helper resolves token commands and may probe filters; credential-free storage observations need a restricted metadata-only invocation rather than the ordinary helper.
- `registry.List` creates its directory and lock, and `Manager.loadReadOnly` delegates to stores whose reads can create locks or access the network; check transitive effects before using them for inventory.

## Developer report

# ISSUE-392 implementation evidence

Status: **partial implementation; not ready for acceptance or publication**. The report core and read-only primitives are implemented. The approved plan's bounded backend/state integration and complete adversarial verification remain unfinished. Unknown evidence is preserved; this artifact does not approve a smaller WorkUnit or claim completion.

## Implemented behavior and boundaries

- `swarm storage report` and `--json` render the same snapshot. The root pre-run bypasses repository normalization, creating registry CRUD and node-profile resolution for this command; `--fork` is rejected. Repository selectors coexist with host-wide cache and temporary-directory candidate discovery. No apply option exists.
- New `internal/storage` scans existing agent-build, validate-build, legacy go-build, agent-deps, validate-deps, managed physical/registered worktrees, local Swarm branches, shared Git objects and recognized scratch candidates. Cache repository association uses the common-directory hash. Unproven keys and prefix-only scratch remain unknown.
- Default limits are 256 repositories, 10,000 resources, 100,000 entry admissions, 100,000 inode identities and 64 MiB of conservative accounted working data. Scanning is sequential, with cancellation checked at each entry and Git boundary. Depth and Git output are independently capped. Partial observations mark the snapshot incomplete and retain only a labeled observed allocation subtotal.
- Logical usage is separate from filesystem-block observations. Global device/inode identity deduplicates physical observations across resources. Branches have no independent byte total. Unsupported or exhausted physical identity coverage leaves the aggregate unknown.
- `registry.ReadSnapshot` reads existing files through safefs without creating a directory or lock. YAML input is capped before reading and parser space is reserved before decoding. Aliases, flow syntax, oversized fields and deep indentation are rejected conservatively. Oversized or unsupported documents produce incomplete evidence. This is bounded whole-document YAML decoding, **not the approved plan's incremental registry parser**.
- `storageuse.Observe` reads supplied trusted control roots without locks, creation or recency updates. It validates version, resource identity, timestamps and tokens, and never returns raw tokens. Complete finished coverage can support advisory build-cache eligibility; unresolved uses block. The CLI does not invent a control-root setting or infer a convention absent from producers. Ordinary CLI cache activity therefore remains unknown when no discoverable use coverage exists.
- A new credential-free Git metadata helper admits only exact local rev-parse, worktree-list and ref-list forms. It disables hooks, fsmonitor, automatic maintenance, global/system configuration and inherited credential variables. It does not invoke token commands. The ordinary credential-bearing helper is unchanged.
- `safefs.Root.Lstat` provides metadata-only, parent-pinned observations without opening hardlinked file contents. Accounting rejects symlinks and special files. Complete use records cannot preserve eligible status after filesystem inspection fails or an entry becomes a symlink.
- Operator examples and a single issue changelog fragment were added. No protected files, approved active inputs, workflow state, leases, registry records or producer lifecycle were intentionally changed. No staging/publication command was executed.

## Remaining approved work

1. Add the optional bounded PR visitor for GitHub and local trackers, plus a bounded authoritative-state preview. The current report makes **zero PR/API calls** and does not acquire authenticated managers; it does not yet provide the approved shared repository retention snapshot.
2. Add bounded workspace/lease inventory inspection paths. Existing cleanup APIs and their authority remain unchanged. Dirty worktrees, active claims, pending submission/revision state and completed PR outcomes are not fully classified; they remain unknown instead of being granted eligibility. Git locked registrations are reported as blocked.
3. Union indexed use/control registrations with discovered directories, including registered resources whose repository directory has disappeared. Existing CLI root discovery cannot discover a storageuse control-root convention that producers do not supply.
4. Complete deterministic injected-adapter verification at every default limit, input/parser/renderer memory admission, API page/error limits, repository-alias selection and registry truncation. The current budget tests are useful focused regressions, not proof of every acceptance bound or the exact 64 MiB working-set claim. Fixed runtime/library buffers still need explicit accounting review.
5. Complete cross-device, sparse/external-hardlink, moving-file, macOS and unsupported-platform fixtures, hook-execution and full authoritative-state no-mutation fixtures. Current fixtures cover real hardlinks, Git index/refs, cache metadata, symlink rejection, cancellation, usage unknowns and writable legacy anchors.
6. Resolve full-suite timeout observations and obtain acceptance-required passing final `make check`. This run cannot claim acceptance criteria 1–7 complete.

## Source and environment evidence

Read SYSTEM_PROMPT.md and WORKUNIT.md first, then PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md, REVIEW.md (`VERDICT: APPROVED`) and the `/swarm-implement` command source. The snapshot has no Git metadata; `git status --short` failed with “not a git repository.” New file absence was checked in the supplied tree; verification at approved base_sha was unavailable. Parent #378 context remains unavailable.

A non-test import search for storageuse finds only the new inventory consumer. Existing producers do not currently expose discoverable use evidence in this source snapshot. Missing evidence has not been converted to inactivity or abandonment.

## Validation observations

Logs and scratch output are under TMPDIR, outside the workspace. Early probe wall times were not independently captured; package durations below are exact Go-reported durations. No uncaptured elapsed time is represented as an exact wall time.

Final focused verification, after the filesystem-substitution fix and preservation of the existing fork-remote flag validation:

| Exact command | Result | Elapsed wall time |
